User Story: As a technical team member, I want to download and clean the FIRMS archive for MODIS (2000–present) and VIIRS (2012–present), so that we have a single, consistent dataset.
Acceptance Criteria: MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS (S-NPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21) data downloaded for the pilot region; hotspots filtered by confidence level; static sources (gas flares, industry) removed using the 'type' field; common column schema for both sensors.

User Story: As a technical team member, I want to aggregate hotspots onto a regular grid (cell × day), so that both sensors can be compared in the same unit despite their different resolutions (1 km vs 375 m).
Acceptance Criteria: Grid defined (e.g. 0.1° or 0.25°); 'fire cell-days' metric computed per sensor; output stored in Parquet/DuckDB; duplicates across VIIRS satellites handled.

User Story: As a scientist, I want the MODIS–VIIRS relationship to be calibrated over the overlap period (2012–present), by region and by month, so that the MODIS record can be converted into a VIIRS-equivalent series.
Acceptance Criteria: Calibration model (regression or quantile mapping) fitted per region/season; Aqua vs S-NPP/NOAA-20 pairing preferred (~13:30 overpass); calibration factors stored and reproducible.

User Story: As a scientist, I want to see validation metrics for the harmonization, so that I can trust the combined series does not introduce bias.
Acceptance Criteria: Overlap years held out for testing; error (e.g. RMSE, bias) reported; before/after harmonization plot available.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want a continuous time series from 2000 to today with no visible break at the MODIS→VIIRS transition, so that I can compare recent years with the past without worrying about the source sensor.
Acceptance Criteria: Single series per region; no artificial discontinuity in 2012 in the charts; the user does not need to choose a sensor.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want to draw an area of interest on the map, so that I can analyse fire activity in exactly the area I care about.
Acceptance Criteria: Interactive map with polygon/rectangle drawing tool; the drawn area is used in all analyses; area can be cleared and redrawn.

User Story: As a land manager, I want to enter coordinates (lat/lon with a radius, or a bounding box), so that I can define the region precisely without drawing by hand.
Acceptance Criteria: Lat/lon fields validated; configurable radius or box; the region is drawn on the map.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want to choose a date range, so that I can focus the analysis on a specific period.
Acceptance Criteria: Start/end date picker between 2000 and the present; invalid values blocked; analyses and exports respect the selected range.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want to see an activity calendar (year × month) with the number of harmonized hotspots, so that I can quickly identify the months and years with the most fire.
Acceptance Criteria: Heatmap with years as rows and months as columns; each cell shows the harmonized count; updates with the selected region and dates.

User Story: As a firefighter, I want the calendar to use an accessible colour ramp with a clear legend, so that I can read the intensity even with colour blindness.
Acceptance Criteria: Accessible sequential ramp (e.g. viridis/cividis); legend with values; contrast checked; not colour-only (values visible on hover/in a table).

User Story: As a land manager, I want to see the exact value when hovering over a calendar cell, so that I get precise numbers without leaving the view.
Acceptance Criteria: Tooltip with month, year, harmonized count and difference from the median.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want to compare the current month's activity with the historical median for the same month, so that I can tell whether the situation is above normal.
Acceptance Criteria: Current month vs median indicator (absolute and %); visual highlight above a threshold (e.g. 90th percentile).

User Story: As a scientist, I want to see the anomalies of each month/year against the multi-year mean or median, so that I can study trends and extreme events.
Acceptance Criteria: Anomaly chart over time; choice between mean and median; reference period stated.

User Story: As a land manager, I want to see the region's average seasonal profile (with its range of variation), so that I can plan resources and prevention throughout the year.
Acceptance Criteria: Monthly chart with median and percentiles (e.g. P10–P90); current month overlaid.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want a ranking of the years and months with the highest activity, so that I can quickly answer 'when was it worst?'.
Acceptance Criteria: Top-N years and top-N months with counts; updates with the selected region.

User Story: As a scientist, I want to download the harmonized hotspots from my search as a CSV, so that I can run my own analyses.
Acceptance Criteria: Download button; CSV with date, lat, lon, sensor/satellite, confidence, FRP and harmonization flag; respects region and dates.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want to export the charts and the aggregated table, so that I can include them in reports and briefings.
Acceptance Criteria: PNG download of charts and CSV of the year × month table.

User Story: As a scientist, I want a page explaining the harmonization method and its limitations, so that I can judge how reliable the results are.
Acceptance Criteria: 'About the method' page with data sources, steps, validation and limitations (e.g. Terra/Aqua orbital drift).

User Story: As a firefighter, I want to see individual hotspots on the map for the chosen period, so that I can locate where activity was concentrated.
Acceptance Criteria: Points or clusters on the map; date filter; acceptable performance with many points (clustering).

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want the data to include the most recent days (near real-time), so that I can compare the current situation with the historical record.
Acceptance Criteria: Ingestion of FIRMS NRT data (API with MAP_KEY); last update date visible in the app.

User Story: As an emergency manager, I want the analysis for a region to appear within a few seconds, so that I can use it during an incident response.
Acceptance Criteria: Response < ~3 s for a country-sized region (pre-computed aggregated data).

User Story: As a firefighter in the field, I want to use the application on a tablet or phone, so that I can check the fire history away from the office.
Acceptance Criteria: Responsive layout; map and calendar usable on small screens.
